method: After freezing, started again with the dated UvA diagram, the current study table and workbook rows. Rechecked annual totals, the 3 EC discrepancy, the normal and extended research choices, progression, and the specific course content behind each proposed match before comparing the canonical.
findings: UvA Biomedical Sciences, RIO 56990, is the Dutch-language, full-time 180 EC bachelor. Its first two years are compulsory. Use the 2026–2027 curriculum PDF for the 3 EC biomedical data science course, which the live HTML lists with a dash. First year is 60 EC, second year is 60 EC, and the selected third year is 30 EC Frontiers in Medical Biology, 12 EC open electives and an 18 EC project. Frontiers comprises 12 and 6 EC taught blocks, 6 EC experimental genomics and 6 EC restricted choice. Keep the 6 and 12 EC slots open. The extended 30 EC project replaces the 12 EC elective block and is a distinct route, as are a minor or exchange in place of specialisation. Frontiers extends the general molecular and experimental identity more broadly than the nervous-system or clinically oriented options.

The official year-one programme moves from cells, genetics, microbes and statistics to anatomy, physiology and disease. The year-two laboratory sequence combines biochemistry and cell biology with molecular techniques and immunology, before microscopy, genome analysis and the mini-thesis. The dated diagram places the Frontiers and genomics modules in the first semester of year three before electives and the project. The current study page describes independent research in a placement and an English report. The UvA accreditation report for ISAT 56990 records completion of the first two years before the research placement. The regular 60+60 EC preceding sequence meets that threshold. The accreditation report is corroboration for progression only. Use the 2026–2027 sources for module identities and credits.

The workbook independently supports laboratory DNA isolation, PCR and electrophoresis, human organ-system function, molecular control of cells, host defence and evolution. The strongest comparisons are accordingly restricted to those or equally well documented subjects. No positive alignment is assigned to elective space, the research placement, omics or general ethics. The only planned image-analysis terms in the six-term horizon are the second and sixth semesters, and the second follows introductory programming. The optional UCR research row has 15 EC and is outside all schedule totals.

The closest option moves from cells and evolutionary genetics to physiology, biochemistry and anatomy, then lab techniques, immunity, pathology and pharmacology. The lab includes PCR, culture, DNA and proteins, without covering a full wet-lab omics or live-cell microscopy sequence. Quantitative and ethical courses support research. The population option builds from epidemiology and human biology into qualitative methods, policy, health behaviour and intervention evidence. Public economics offers public goods and policy tools, not a dedicated health-financing course. The quantitative option uses general image processing, linear systems, numerical differential equations, statistics and machine learning alongside molecular and physiological study. It teaches transferable methods rather than a specialist genomics or personalised-treatment sequence. Description-only Perception & Action examines sensory and motor mechanisms and supports the closest option. Comparative neurobiology, perception and cognition could support a fourth direction, but their strongest contributions already appear within the closest programme. Each retained option has a separate question and course spine. Removed inaccurate VU notes, shifted imaging into an offered spring term and improved the laboratory sequence. Only the nine positive rows with identifiable shared subject matter remain paired. The research placement and optional UCR independent research remain clearly distinct.
